candidate.title: RBNS
candidate.scope: RNA Bind-n-Seq (RBNS), the assigned poster row: random RNA and SBP-tagged RBP binding at varied protein concentrations, streptavidin-bead capture, RNA purification, and reverse transcription/amplification to cDNA. Concentration conditions remain distinct; no pooling is depicted. The RBNS overview in Lambert et al. (2014) clarifies the sequenced carrier and interpretation. Neighboring hiCLIP and TRIBE rows and the chemical legend are outside this target. Sequencing and input-library comparison are paper-supported readout context, not additional depicted operations.

operations.label: Bead coated with streptavidin
operations.description: Capture tagged RBP and its associated RNA on streptavidin-coated beads. The bead panel changes the attachment state of the complexes while depicting free material around them.
operations.mechanism: Streptavidin binds the streptavidin-binding peptide carried by the RBP.
operations.information_effect: Retains the RNA–RBP association physically on the bead. Capture is mediated by the protein tag, rather than an RNA tag.

operations.label: Purify
operations.description: Recover the RNA from captured complexes, separating it from bead/protein and unbound material. The output is the isolated RNA segment shown before reverse transcription.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper describes recovery and extraction of bead-selected RNA; the schematic leaves this as a broad purification block.
operations.information_effect: Enriches sequences recovered with the RBP. Recovery alone does not imply that every retained RNA is a specific high-affinity ligand.

evidence.quote: Unimodal enrichment profiles for highly enriched kmers were observed for RBFOX2, CELF1 and MBNL1, in general agreement with our model under the assumption of moderate levels of nonspecific background (Fig. 2D).

operations.label: Reverse transcription amplification
operations.description: Convert the purified RNA into cDNA and amplify it. The paper identifies PCR as the amplification step and describes addition of barcoded sequencing adapters.
operations.information_effect: The sequenced carrier is DNA derived from selected RNA, preserving RNA sequence identity through copying. The paper compares motif frequencies in the selected library with those in the input library to infer the tested RBP’s in vitro binding preferences. Selected-library recovery does not directly map endogenous cellular binding positions. The poster row ends at cDNA; sequencing and input-library comparison are paper-supported readout context rather than drawn operations.

evidence.quote: We adapted the general approach used by HT-SELEX and Bind-n-Seq to the study of protein-RNA interactions in vitro in a method we call “RNA Bind-n-Seq” (RBNS).
evidence.rationale: The assay binds purified protein to an artificial random RNA pool and reads selected sequence frequencies. Those molecules do not carry the original cellular transcript coordinates needed for an endogenous occupancy map.
